items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Why shouldn't he tell the term of that? He's probably talking about Ammons and Johnson. [INTERVIEWEE] It might have been Ammons and Johnson, or Johnson and Turner. Who was it? There's a couple of them that were playing around New York. Yeah, they were around.

ctx.x: Kansas City Jazz. I don't know whether you read it or not. I wrote that first little thing I wrote for the record changer was just a little paragraph about Johnny being in New York. And he went to a nightclub where a couple of boogie woogie players were the star attraction. I guess they were the only thing there. And they were playing the boogie woogie stuff. And Johnny got persuaded to give a few examples of his stuff. You know, he played and went over all right. And he was telling Lomax about playing there, you…
Why shouldn't he tell the term of that? He's probably talking about Ammons and Johnson.

It might have been Ammons and Johnson, or Johnson and Turner. Who was it? There's a couple of them that were playing around New York. Yeah, they were around. Anyhow, the guys that only know one, too. That's what got it with Handy, too, you know. Because Handy hadn't really done something with it. The blues made plenty of money out of it. Johnny said, blues wasn't considered music in those days, which was a fact. They'd hush you up as you started playing it down there and go on and that kind of thing. And also, I…
